# Does an armor-first pick text (Starch Plating, then max HP) raise survival from 0:00?

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | done |
| Area | models |
| Result | refuted |
| Created | L4.I5 |
| Updated | L4.I6 |

## Hypothesis

The 3-item games lived 5 of 5 with Starch Plating 5/5 by about 2:00-3:30 and 29-61 damage, because porcupine-spud's catalyst made Starch Plating show up and the planner took it. A planner.pick text that ranks Starch Plating first, then shrine Armor or Max HP, then max-HP passives, chest evolutions and top-weapon levels, and takes a new weapon only below 3 held, gives the same armor without handed items. It cuts damage taken by 3:00 and lets more thin builds reach 4:00 and 5:00. Earlier armor and HP pick tests were single games with no chests (B39, B65), so this is the first fair test.

## Method

Seeker-sprouts with the playbook knobs and prompts, only planner.pick changed, 240 s from 0:00 on s31-38. Pair with the playbook games on file for s31-35 (5:00, 5:00, 3:05, 5:00, 2:39) and with new playbook games on s36 and s37. s38 gets an arm game now and a playbook game next iteration. Read Starch Plating level and armor at 2:00 and 3:00, max HP, damage taken by 3:00, chests opened, first evolution, and survival to 4:00. Needs 8 paired seeds with a clear margin before any playbook change.

## Findings

Seeker-sprouts with the armor-first planner.pick, 240 s from 0:00 on s31-38: alive at 4:00 on 2 of 8 (s31, s38) against 4 of 7 for the playbook on s31-37 (3 of 5 on file plus s36 alive and s37 dead played now). Starch Plating was taken at 100% every time offered, but the builds dealt little damage (200-360 kills in the deaths) and 6 of 8 opened 0 chests. Armor without damage does not keep a thin build alive. Not added to the playbook.
